pick.name: Cal.com
pick.what: Scheduling with routing, workflows, teams; Meet/Zoom links
pick.why: Most capable scheduler: routing forms, workflows, teams; free for one user.
pick.free_limits: Free: single user, unlimited event types and calendars, no usage limits; Teams $12/user/mo yearly, Organizations $28
pick.license: proprietary cloud; public repo now MIT 'Cal.diy' (non-production)

best_free.name: Google Calendar appointment schedules
best_free.what: Booking page in Google Calendar with auto Meet links
best_free.why: Zero new vendor and Meet links built in for anyone on Google Calendar; free for one booking page.
best_free.free_limits: Personal account: one booking page; premium features need eligible Workspace or Google One plan (eligibility unverified)

alts.name: Calendly
alts.why: Most familiar to invitees; free plan is one event type.
alts.free_limits: Free: 1 event type, 1 calendar; Standard $10/seat/mo, Teams $16

alts.name: TidyCal
alts.why: Most generous free plan (unlimited booking types) if Google's free tier is too thin.
alts.free_limits: Free forever: unlimited bookings and booking types, 1 calendar, 1% fee on payments

candidates.name: Cal.com
candidates.verdict: pick: most capable, free single user

decision: Cal.com offers the best feature set, including routing and workflows, with a free single-user plan. Google appointment schedules are enough if interviews are one-off on Meet; Calendly if invitees expect it. Cal.com moved its production code private in 2026, so self-host depends on its MIT community edition.
